title: Stress test the professional operating model
learner_promise: Demonstrate a six-part Professional AI Operating Model that works in ordinary tasks, inaccurate outputs, and high-consequence situations; complete Journey One with a feasible capstone charter.

pacing.label: Outdated policy case and consequence review
Three stress tests and a model revision

outcomes: Combine purpose, AI support roles, human responsibilities, review process, responsible boundaries and growth commitments.
Adjust review depth to accuracy, usefulness, suitability, privacy and consequence.
Test a routine case, an inaccurate output and a high-consequence privacy or authority request.
Revise one weak operating rule; name an actual source, reviewer and stop condition.
Defend one proceed and one pause decision; confirm a feasible capstone charter for Journey Two.

teaching.heading: Combine the work into one six-part Professional AI Operating Model
paragraphs: Your earlier Journey One evidence describes the person served, selected need, permitted AI roles, measurable value, professional decision requests and FOCUS charter. Bring these into one practical guide.

The six parts are purpose and outcome; AI support role or no AI; accountable human responsibilities; documented review process; privacy/authority boundaries; and ongoing capability growth. This is a professional working model, not a technical architecture.
teaching.think_prompt: Could another person explain your project's purpose, reviewer and exact stop condition using your six-part model?

teaching.heading: Match review depth to potential consequence
paragraphs: A routine fictional note organization can be checked directly. A customer policy message requires the current authorized source and a named reviewer. Private records, binding commitments or unapproved authority require a pause and an authorized decision maker.
Review for accuracy, usefulness, suitability to affected people, sensitive information and your ability to explain the result. Do not confuse a polished message with a verified one.
teaching.think_prompt: When would an outdated source make a seemingly helpful customer draft unacceptable?

teaching.heading: Stress test against three situations
paragraphs: Test a routine task, an inaccurate AI output and a high-consequence scenario. For each state the safe input, consequence, source check, AI role, human owner, proceed or pause, missing rule and correction.
Do not submit real sensitive data to an AI model for the exercise. Use fictional examples and refuse any unsupported permission or approval the model invents.
teaching.think_prompt: Which specific working rule fails when the model uses yesterday's customer policy?

teaching.heading: Revise the model and explain two human decisions
paragraphs: Replace weak rules such as 'check the answer' with an instruction naming the approved policy source, reviewing person and what happens during uncertainty. Keep original and revised rules together.

Defend a proceed decision on a reversible safe practice task and a pause decision where a current source or authority is missing. Confirm the same FOCUS charter remains finishable for the next journey.
teaching.think_prompt: What must become true before your paused task can responsibly proceed?

worked_case.label: An AI-drafted customer message uses an outdated policy
worked_case.setup: FICTIONAL TRAINING EXAMPLE: An assistant writes a courteous response using a previous service policy. The reply appears finished but does not establish the current approved wording.

evidence_table.claim: The customer message is ready because the text is clear
evidence_table.evidence: Clarity does not establish which policy version governs
evidence_table.action: Require review against the latest approved source.

evidence_table.claim: The model's citation proves the policy is current
evidence_table.evidence: The cited description belongs to an older fictional policy
evidence_table.action: Withhold until current policy is checked and the named reviewer approves.

evidence_table.claim: Any employee may authorize the outgoing statement
evidence_table.evidence: The exercise does not establish service approval authority
evidence_table.action: Name the responsible policy or service owner.

evidence_table.claim: An AI system can decide high-consequence customer outcomes from sensitive records
evidence_table.evidence: No permission or binding decision authority is supplied
evidence_table.action: Do not upload private information; pause and escalate.

worked_case.revised_example: Before any policy-based message is sent, compare it with the latest authorized policy. A named service reviewer confirms both source and language. If the source is uncertain or inconsistent, withhold the message and ask the policy owner to resolve it.
demonstration_steps: Assemble the six-part operating model for the continuing project.
Find the outdated customer policy and replace a vague review rule.
Raise review depth for privacy, permission and binding decisions.
Record a justified proceed, justified pause, revised rule and feasible charter.
worked_case.question: What explicit source, reviewer and hold action does a workable review rule need?

application.heading: Build the original six-part Professional AI Operating Model
application.instruction: Use the same Path A or Path B project to write purpose, AI role, human owner, review, boundaries and growth commitments. Include your Lesson 1.5 FOCUS charter.
application.evidence: Original model grounded in previously saved learner work.

application.heading: Challenge the model through three safe scenarios
application.instruction: Test routine work, an inaccurate response and a high-consequence privacy or authority request with your own AI assistant using sanitized fictional notes. Name proceed/pause decisions, evidence sources, human owners and failure conditions.
application.evidence: Three scenario records with factual checks and explicit human responsibility.

application.heading: Revise one rule and confirm project direction
application.instruction: Choose one weak boundary or review rule; change it and explain why, or justify the existing rule with evidence. Defend one proceed and one pause decision; confirm your capstone is feasible and approved for only the documented fictional first test.
application.evidence: Original/revised model, correction rationale, opportunity brief and confirmed charter.

approved_ai_request: Challenge this operating model with a routine case, an inaccurate response and a high-consequence request. Identify weaknesses and missing human owners. Suggest corrections for my review. Model: [sanitized draft].
responsibility_map_fields: AI support role and no-AI boundary

verification.heading: Show one justified proceed
verification.prompt: Explain why a limited fictional routine task may continue and name the authorized reviewer.

verification.heading: Show one justified pause
verification.prompt: Explain the missing policy, permission or authority, human escalation and evidence required before resuming.

verification.heading: Defend the changed rule and feasible capstone
verification.prompt: Show original and revised rule, what changed and why, and confirm the Journey 1 charter remains finishable.

completion_criteria: Six-part operating model assembled with named human review and boundaries
Three scenario tests including one privacy or authority failure
A revised or evidence-justified operating rule with explanation
A defensible proceed decision and a defensible pause decision
Feasible capstone charter and continuing Journey One project evidence preserved
handoff: Journey One concludes with a tested Professional AI Operating Model and realistic FOCUS charter. Carry both into Journey Two: Build AI into Business Workflows, only when that journey becomes available under the approved curriculum schedule.
